title: Neon Courier: Data Run
premise: Pilot a glowing courier craft through a procedurally shifting cyber-firewall tunnel, surviving as long as possible while delivering data packets through an accelerating stream.
interaction_model: Single-input hold-and-release control: hold/touch/press to climb, release to descend, with start and restart buttons outside the active run.
objective: Stay inside the moving tunnel gap, avoid wall segments and spike hazards, survive the rising speed curve, and achieve the highest possible packet score.
progression: Endless score-chasing progression with increasing scroll speed, shrinking tunnel gaps, periodic danger warnings, and later-run spike hazards; each run ends on collision or leaving bounds, followed by instant retry.
mood: Fast, tense, stylish, glowing, futuristic, and replay-driven.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short-session arcade reflex games
fans of endless runners and dodge-survival games
mobile and browser players who prefer simple one-touch controls
players drawn to neon sci-fi presentation
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is an endless survival dodging game centered on one-button vertical control.
High confidence in the cyberpunk courier/data-stream theme because the UI text, score labels, and visuals all reinforce it.
Moderate confidence that the best mechanical comparison is runner-style survival rather than a pure shooter or platformer, since the player does not attack and remains horizontally fixed.
Low confidence on any deeper fiction beyond the courier/firewall motif because the game contains no story scenes or narrative progression.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser arcade game called "Neon Courier: Data Run" where the player pilots a small glowing courier ship through an endless side-scrolling cyberpunk tunnel. The ship stays at a fixed horizontal position while the world scrolls from right to left, and the entire control scheme is a single continuous input: hold mouse or touch to make the ship climb, release to let it descend. Build the core gameplay around surviving inside a procedurally generated corridor made from paired top and bottom wall segments that leave a moving gap; the tunnel center should drift in different patterns such as smooth movement, jagged zig-zags, and tighter narrow sections. Make the run get harder over time by steadily increasing scroll speed and shrinking the safe gap, then introduce occasional glowing spike hazards later in the run. End the run instantly if the ship hits a wall, spike, or screen boundary. Present score as delivered packets and track a persistent best run. Use a strong neon sci-fi presentation: dark background, moving grid lines, soft parallax energy waves, bright cyan/indigo/pink glow, a futuristic HUD, and a sleek courier craft with a trailing light ribbon and tilt animation based on ascent or descent. Add a start screen and a game-over screen with stylish cyberpunk wording, quick restart flow, warning callouts when speed surges occur, celebratory feedback on score milestones, and punchy audio cues for start, warning, scoring, and crashing. The overall feel should be tense, responsive, readable on desktop and mobile, and built for short replayable high-score sessions.
